analysis: The broad arts option combines visual analysis, modern art, museum studies, art historiography, sociology and film. Renaissance connections and African heritage provide specific alternatives to a single Western account of art. Gender history and media representation explain how art participates in public life. Qualitative work provides practical cultural research methods. The arts-specific art historiography course and gender-history study make a closer contribution than a US-centred history research seminar.

The film and communication option gives added weight to film adaptation, documentary production, critical readings, popular media, persuasion and rhetoric. It shares analytic foundations with the broad option but differs by six courses in each direction. Popular media is a more direct contribution than a second general philosophy course. Documentary and creative communication provide real practice without implying a professional film placement.

The policy option combines study of museums, heritage, race and representation with audience research, economics and management. Policy Analysis provides memo-writing and a framework for tracing policy decisions; its principal case is not about the arts. Digital strategy contributes a method for studying organisational change. Arts courses and museum practice keep these methods connected to the relevant cultural sector.

Three plans differ by 45, 97.5 and 112.5 EC each way. The existing schedules passed availability checks; revisions improve contribution and sequencing. Film analysis, intermedial adaptation, exhibition and documentary production support partial alignments. Dedicated music history and theory, separate film history and theory, professional arts criticism and an advanced film seminar retain visible unmatched rows. UCR optional research stays separate from the required Groningen thesis.
constructionStop: Three coherent, distinct options reach the programme limit.
